title: Adaptive KV lifecycle, pin-decay strategy, and profile curation for long-context models
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Background: As more customer workloads push models with long prompt+chat histories, our KV cache occupancy and hit-rate dynamics vary significantly by model architecture and sequence-length distribution. Current onboarding pins a model version to a single KV retention policy, which leads to either over-retention (wasted memory/cost) or under-retention (missed hits and higher latency for long-context requests). Goal: implement an adaptive lifecycle and pin-decay strategy plus a curated profile publishing workflow so every model-version ships with a stable initial policy that evolves deterministically from observed sequence clusters. This ticket covers the runtime changes, telemetry, onboarding tooling, and console artifacts needed for safe rollout and rollback.
acceptance_criteria: 1) A new pin-decay policy is implemented in the runtime: per-model-version TTL + decay multiplier that reduces retention for cold sequence clusters; 2) Model onboarding flow publishes a curated profile JSON into the profiles registry (includes sequence-cluster centroids, retention targets, warmup hints); 3) Console shows per-model predicted memory and expected steady-state hit-rate before and after applying curated policy; 4) Telemetry exposes signals for early-warning (hit-rate drop > 8% over 1 hour, unexpected mem growth > 12%); 5) Can perform canary with rollback via policy override; 6) Unit + integration tests and a data-driven experiment demonstrate cost savings >= 10% for long-context workloads without >2% regressions in tail latency.
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (Spike, done): sample long-context traces and produce sequence-cluster VM to evaluate retention utility; Phase 2 (Runtime core): add TTL+decay hook in KV allocator, implement deterministic decay schedule and stable seeding for reproducible behavior across nodes; Phase 3 (Onboarding tooling): profile-curation service that ingests sampled traces and emits profile JSON; Phase 4 (Console + API): surface curated policy, allow manual override and staged rollout controls; Phase 5 (Rollout): internal canary, partner beta, full production. See PR and design links in 'links'.
telemetry_signals: Emit the following metrics at model-version granularity: kv_hit_rate, kv_miss_reason (prefetch|eviction|cold-start), kv_mem_bytes, kv_retention_ttl_seconds, seq_cluster_id, seq_cluster_cnt, tail_latency_p95/p99. Instrument a derived metric: expected_savings_pct = baseline_token_cost - projected_token_cost_with_profile. Add alert rules: kv_hit_rate_drop_rx (>=8% over 60m), kv_mem_growth_spike (>=12% over 30m), seq_cluster_shift (dominant cluster change >40% in 24h).
migration_plan: Start with non-customer-facing internal model pool (internal-lab). Generate curated profiles for top-10 long-context models. Canary rollouts in us-west-2 for 10% of traffic per model-version with autoscaling off. Run for 72 hours and validate telemetry. Next expand to partner customers upon success, then to all traffic. Maintain a forced-policy override route per model-version to revert to previous retention TTL. Include a staged automated rollback if hit-rate drop alert fires twice within 2 hours.
qa_plan: Unit tests for decay math and deterministic seeding. Integration test harness that replays sampled traces under both baseline and new policy and asserts hit-rate and latency invariants. Synthetic workload tests to verify memory bounds under worst-case sequences. End-to-end canary test: deploy to canary cluster, run scripted traffic for 72h, capture Grafana dashboard snapshots and compare against baseline run. Document manual test checklist in Confluence.
